settings.smtp_which_help: Small churches can often use the mailbox of their own domain. For larger lists, consider Amazon SES (very cheap), or the free SMTP plans of Brevo or Mailjet. Koinonia works with any provider that offers SMTP.

deliv.intro: To make sure your emails arrive in the inbox and not in spam, your domain {domain} needs three DNS records. Your web host or IT volunteer can add them in a few minutes.
deliv.builtin_title: What Koinonia already does for you
deliv.builtin_1: One-click unsubscribe headers (RFC 8058), as required by Gmail and Yahoo since 2024.
deliv.builtin_2: A plain-text version alongside every HTML email.
deliv.builtin_3: Sending gradually, at the pace you set.
deliv.builtin_4: Addresses that bounce permanently are no longer emailed.
deliv.builtin_5: Double opt-in, so your list contains only real, willing readers.
deliv.spf_text: States which servers may send email for {domain}. Your provider tells you the exact value; there may be only one SPF record.
deliv.dkim_text: A digital signature that proves an email really comes from {domain}. You get the record (a long key) from your mail provider.
deliv.dkim_value: (the key your provider gives you, e.g. at selector._domainkey)
deliv.dmarc_text: Tells receiving servers what to do with emails that fail SPF or DKIM. Start with p=none and tighten it later. Add it at _dmarc.{domain}.
